$comment: Proposed assertsLaw classification for every clause, made by reading each clause body against one question: does it tell the reader what the LAW REQUIRES (authority) or what the PARTIES AGREE (drafting)? The operative test is descriptive versus performative. "Such provisions are void under California law" describes the law and belongs on the authority track. "This handbook is not a contract" tries to make something so — it is the instrument speaking, not a report about the law — and belongs on the drafting track. A clause that merely defers ("as required by the law of X") asserts nothing and is drafting. Recorded as a per-document default plus explicit exceptions, so the rule applied is visible and auditable rather than 360 opaque calls. These are proposals. Nothing is applied until a named person accepts them.

msa.why: A master services agreement is a negotiated instrument. The only clauses that state law are the California compliance overlays, which exist precisely to tell the reader what California requires.

governance.why: An operating agreement or bylaws is negotiated. The exceptions state background law the parties cannot vary: the LLC act's default rules, charging-order exclusivity, the fiduciary standard of care, HIPAA business-associate agreements, mechanics-lien preliminary notices, professional licensing, and the duty to publish a privacy notice.

charter.why: Charter text is drafted, but the purpose clause recites the statutory formula, and the New York publication and California professional-services clauses state what those states require.

consent.why: Initial consents are corporate authorisations the founders adopt. The 83(b) acknowledgement is different: it tells the reader what the Internal Revenue Code requires and when.

ip-assignment.why: An assignment is negotiated. Work-made-for-hire status is a matter of copyright law, and the state carve-out states the statutory limit on what an assignment can reach.

vesting.why: Vesting schedules, Cause definitions, repurchase rights and transfer restrictions are all negotiated terms. Nothing here states law.

foreign-qualification.why: Qualifying in another state is a set of things that state requires — a registered agent with a physical address, a recent certificate of good standing, an assumed name if yours is taken, revenue-agency registration. The application text itself is form content.

election-83b.why: The election, its filing deadline and the community-property spouse rule are all creatures of the Internal Revenue Code.

schedules.why: Schedules and exhibits are form content the parties fill in.

ca-notices.why: This document exists to tell the reader what California requires of an employer. Every clause in it is a statement of law, including the six that were classified as drafting: the benefit-notice and posting lists are statutory distribution duties, the two local-ordinance clauses assert that the more employee-favourable provision governs, and the proactive-audit clause rests its whole value on the PAGA penalty reduction for pre-notice compliance.

handbook.why: A handbook is mostly a restatement of statutory entitlements — overtime, meal and rest, leave, records — so the default is authority. The three exceptions are the Company speaking for itself: the purpose and no-contract statement and the acknowledgment are operative disclaimers, and the anti-harassment section states the Company's own policy and reporting channels rather than what the law requires (can_harassment_policy carries that).

employment-agreement.why: An offer letter is a negotiated instrument, so the default is drafting. The exceptions are the clauses that describe the law rather than operate: the California overlays, the statement that a representative PAGA waiver is generally unenforceable, that the terms follow the state where work is actually performed, that unapproved overtime is still payable, the 83(b) deadline, that section 2802 reimbursement applies regardless of policy, that non-competes are void, that salary alone does not establish exempt status, and that final wages may not be withheld to force return of property.

employment.why: This is the employment-policy manual, and most of it restates statutory duties — registration, overtime, meal and rest, final pay, wage statements, sick leave, the non-compete prohibition. The exceptions are the Company's own practice: the at-will disclaimer is operative, the written-offer requirement and the contractor pre-engagement review are internal procedure, and the anti-harassment policy states the Company's channels rather than the regulation behind them.

compliance-calendar.why: A compliance calendar is nothing but statements of what the law requires and when. That includes the three previously marked drafting: EIN and state tax registration, the formation state's annual-report schedule, and payroll tax deposits and Forms 940/941, each of which asserts a filing duty and, in the payroll case, personal liability for trust fund taxes.

dpa.why: A data processing addendum is a contract: instructions, security measures, audit rights, subprocessor notice, transfers and liability are all negotiated. The exceptions describe law the contract cannot change — the CCPA service-provider conditions, the statutory definition of sensitive personal information, the deletion chain and its exceptions, the notice-at-collection purpose limitation, and the fact that controller status follows the purpose of the processing rather than the label the parties give it.

contractor-agreement.why: The engagement terms themselves are negotiated, but this document carries an unusual amount of law because misclassification is its central risk. The exceptions state it: the ABC test and its statutory exemptions, the Freelance Worker Protection Act, reimbursement exposure on reclassification, that a recital of independence does not establish it, that prompt-payment statutes may penalise late payment, that contractor work is generally not work made for hire so the express assignment is what transfers ownership, the whistleblower carve-out, and that a waiver of benefits does not stop an agency reclassifying the relationship.

sow.why: A statement of work is scope, schedule, fees, dependencies and change control — all negotiated. Only the prevailing-wage clause states law: what makes a project a public work, registration with the Department of Industrial Relations, certified payroll, and per-worker per-day penalties.

nda.why: A mutual NDA is a negotiated instrument end to end, including compelled disclosure and return-or-destruction, which are operative permissions rather than statements of law. The one exception is the personnel non-solicit, whose closing sentence asserts that the provision is unenforceable against employees working in California — the same claim ea_noncompete_void makes, and it belongs on the same track.

deferralsReviewed.$comment: lawTalk() is a surface matcher: it fires on phrases like "required by law" and "statutory" wherever they appear. Every clause below is proposed as drafting and trips it. Each was re-read, and each turned out to be a DEFERRAL — the clause names the law as a condition or a limit without saying what the law contains, so there is no assertion to check against a statute. That is the drafting case, not an exception to it. The list is explicit so the check cannot be waved through in bulk: a clause that trips lawTalk and is not named here fails the run.
deferralsReviewed.msa_marks: "either Party may make disclosures required by law" — a carve-out from a consent requirement. Says nothing about what law compels.
deferralsReviewed.msa_breach_notify: The seventy-two hours is a contractual deadline, not a statutory one. "any notification obligation" and "unless required by law" both point outward without content.
deferralsReviewed.gov_dataproc: "within the statutory deadline applicable in {{opStateLong}}" names a deadline it does not state. The security programme and vendor DPA duties are covenants the Company gives, not law it reports.
deferralsReviewed.ea_ip: "subject to any statutory carve-out required in {{opStateLong}}" defers to ipa_state_carveout, which is on the authority track and carries the section 2870 content.
deferralsReviewed.dpa_assistance: "within the statutory period" — the obligation created is to assist; the period itself is left to the law.
deferralsReviewed.dpa_deletion: "Copies retained in backup media or required by law" is an exception to a contractual deletion duty.
deferralsReviewed.nda_compelled: "required by law or valid legal process" is the trigger for a contractual permission. The clause does not say when disclosure is compelled.
deferralsReviewed.nda_return: "copies required by law" — same shape: an exception to the contractual return duty.
deferralsReviewed.sh_return_property: "copies required by law or held in routine backup systems" — an exception to a contractual return duty, in the shared General Provisions block. Names the law as a limit without saying what it requires, which is the deferral shape, not an assertion.
